The test image shows a **longitudinally split soybean stem** held in hand, with the following features:
- Green, hairy exterior (normal-appearing outside)
- **Clear brown/amber discoloration of the internal pith** running the length of the stem
- No external lesions, pycnidia, or mold visible

This is the classic diagnostic sign for **Brown Stem Rot** — splitting the stem to reveal brown pith. The key distinguishing feature from Sudden Death Syndrome (not in the 10-class list anyway) is that the pith turns **brown** (SDS keeps white pith). Anthracnose shows external dark acervuli on pods/stems. Diaporthe shows external linear pycnidia. None of the other candidates (viral diseases, damping-off, rust) produce internal stem pith discoloration.
